newsitem.title: UK: SWIMMING-WORLD BEST FOR HAN, CLOSE CALL BY KLIM.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-WORLD BEST FOR HAN, CLOSE CALL BY KLIM.

text.p: China's Han Xue bettered one world mark and Australia's Michael Klim swam within an ace of another in a lively final session in the British leg of the World Cup on Wednesday.

Han, 15, improved on her own short-course world best for the women's 50 metres breaststroke, sprinting strongly away from her rivals to win by more than a second in 30.88 seconds and slice 0.10 of a second from the time she set in Beijing in January last year.
"The record was her own, so I'm not surprised," coach Zhao Ge said. "She is a very good short-course swimmer because she has a lot of power."
Klim crowned a magnificent two days for himself and Australia in the fifth leg of the eight-venue World Cup series with his fourth victory in the new Tollcross Park pool.
Klim, victor of Tuesday's 100 metres freestyle and 50 butterfly, dominated Wednesday's 200 freestyle and shortly afterwards came within a whisker of a world record in the 100 butterfly.
The 19-year-old Australian surged through the 100 butterfly in 52.09, finishing just 0.02 outside the world mark set by Marcel Gery of Canada in February 1990.

Behind Klim, Britain's James Hickman claimed a European short-course record of 52.34, beating the 52.51 posted by Germany's Michael Gross in Aachen in March 1990 and equalled by Ukraine's Denis Silantiev in Espoo, Finland, last week.
Hickman, who is just back from a training camp in Australia and won Tuesday's 200 butterfly in national record time, said his instant reaction was disappointment he had been beaten.
"Then I looked up -- European record time and it doesn't matter if I'm beaten on this occasion," he said.
Gross, who lost his 800 freestyle short-course record to former East German Joerg Hoffmann in Malmo, Sweden, last Sunday, has now been deprived of all his individual world and European marks.
Australia, enjoying a successful spree on the World Cup circuit, were the most prolific winners with 11 victories in the 34 events of the two-day meeting.
Klim's four triumphs were backed by a superb hat-trick of freestyle golds for 14-year-old Natasha Bowron, who trounced her rivals in Wednesday's 400 metres after prevailing in Tuesday's 200 and 800.
"This is my first national team experience so I'm really pleased with how I've done so far," Bowron said.
Fellow Australians Adrian Radley and Matthew Dunn completed respective doubles in backstroke and individual medley.
Han capped an impressive two days for China's women swimmers, who appear to have put the relative disappointment of last year's Atlanta Olympics behind them as they seek to return to former heights.
Liu Limin, double long-course world champion, swam a formidably strong 200 butterfly in 2:06.85 after swimming the second-fastest women's short-course 100 butterfly ever on Tuesday.
But compatriot Lu Bin, competing abroad for the first time since serving a two-year drugs ban, was denied a golden double by disqualification.
Lu, winner of Tuesday's 50 backstroke, touched first in the 100 backstroke but was disqualified for illegally kicking at the first turn. She later finished third in the 100 metres individual medley.
The next World Cup event is in Gelsenkirchen, Germany, on Saturday and Sunday.
